key_insight: The paper argues that medical AI should move beyond static diagnosis toward world models that simulate how patient states change over time and how interventions may alter future trajectories.
clinical_relevance: Such models could help clinicians anticipate deterioration, compare treatment-conditioned futures, and personalize care decisions for individual patients.
method: Construct patient states from longitudinal, multimodal medical data.
Model clinical dynamics as an internal simulator of disease progression.
Use intervention-aware planning to support treatment decisions and digital-twin style forecasting.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review and roadmap that synthesizes representative systems across foundation models, longitudinal modelling, disease simulation, treatment-effect estimation, reinforcement learning, and digital twins rather than reporting a single experimental dataset.
watch_item: Plausible simulated rollouts may still fail to be clinically useful if the underlying patient-state representations, causal assumptions, and validation against real outcomes are weak.
paper_title: Medical world models: representing medical states, modelling clinical dynamics and guiding intervention policies
